text: DSH 视频皮肤（DSH 插件，网页和桌面客户端）：为 DSH 界面铺设循环视频聊天背景，并在启动时播放开机动画。它通过宿主注入样式与运行时脚本、提供本地视频和配置路由，并在设置页注册控制卡片。主要功能包括背景透明度调节、开机动画播放与跳过、替换或开关视频素材、背景插件共存让路，以及浅色与深色主题联动。适合希望个性化 DSH 界面并使用自选短片的用户。无需 API 密钥或外部账号；配置与自定义素材保存在 DSH_HOME。

DSH Video Skin adds a looping video backdrop and skippable boot animation. Its settings page controls opacity, custom clips, wallpaper coexistence, and theme behavior. It serves local media; no API key or external account is needed.

怎么调聊天背景的透明程度，让视频明显又不太影响阅读？
希望和其他壁纸插件一起用，检测到对方时自动让出背景
I want a looping video wallpaper behind my DSH conversations.
Can the startup screen play a short animation that I can skip?
I need controls for video opacity and custom background clips in DSH.
Make the chat background yield while another wallpaper plugin is active.
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「循环视频背景」：在 DSH 聊天界面背景中播放静音循环短片，并按深浅主题应用表面透明度和视频蒙版。页面加载后延迟载入背景视频。
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「开机动画」：启动时在界面上方播放视频，可配置声音、结束淡出和点击跳过；遇到浏览器自动播放限制时可回退为静音播放。
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「透明度控制」：点击悬浮控件或打开设置页调节表面与蒙版透明度，预设和重置可用，修改通过本地配置文件保存。
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「自定义视频管理」：通过悬浮面板开关开机动画或背景、上传 MP4/WebM/OGV 视频，也可删除自定义素材并恢复默认视频。
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「壁纸共存」：背景模式设为自动时，检测到其他壁纸插件在运行便让出背景；也可选择始终由本插件接管。
DSH 视频皮肤的功能「主题联动」：可关闭联动、自动切换深色主题，或在页面加载后先询问用户；一次评估后记住选择，并提供恢复入口。
DSH 视频皮肤使用自定义开机动画时，普通浏览器可能阻止带声音的自动播放；运行时会尝试静音继续，并显示单独的声音按钮。
DSH 视频皮肤在桌面端安装后需要完整重启 DSH 才能使启动时收集的界面注入生效；背景透明度设置则可刷新页面后应用。

dsh-video-skin README · dsh-video-skin：[](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

**DSH 视频皮肤**：一段短片循环铺成整个界面的**聊天背景**（无声、透明度界面里就能调），
另一段做**有声的开机动画**（片尾交叉溶解进界面、**点击画面随时跳过**）。**零依赖**。

dsh-video-skin README · 安装（Install）：**设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**，把下面这一行贴进输入框，点「安装」，然后**完全退出并重新打开 DSH**：

```
dsh-video-skin@0.1.6
```

- Prebuilt on npm (current latest `0.1.6`); `dsh-video-skin` without a version follows latest.
- From source: `github:Something11235/dsh-video-skin#main`

> 桌面版（Electron）的索引注入表是**宿主启动时收集一次**的快照，所以装完必须**完全重启 DSH**
> 才会生效（刷新页面不够）。卸载：`dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> remove dsh-video-skin`，
> 或者用仓库里的 `scripts/uninstall.ps1`。

装好之后：右下角会出现一个半透明小圆钮，点开就是**透明度滑块**（调完刷新还在，不用重启）；
启动时会先播放开机动画，**点一下画面**就跳过。

dsh-video-skin README · 安装（Install）：English: install `github:Something11235/dsh-video-skin#main` from **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**,
then **fully quit and relaunch DSH**. A small pill appears in the bottom-right corner for the
transparency sliders; click anywhere during the boot animation to skip it.

dsh-video-skin README · 安装（Install）：A **video skin** for DSH: one clip becomes a looping, silent **video backdrop** behind the whole Web UI,
and a second clip becomes a **boot animation** — **played with sound**, **played through to its end**,
then fading into the app, and **skippable with a click**.

dsh-video-skin README · 安装（Install）：- Boot animation: full-window clip **with audio**, a progress bar driven by the kernel's real activation
  progress, and a permanent “click to skip” pill. The clip **finishes first** (`ended`), then the overlay
  fades out over a **fixed** `fadeMs`; the volume fades with it instead of being cut off.
  > Earlier builds cross-dissolved over the clip's tail and used the *actual remaining time* as the fade
  > duration — when the app became ready late that left only 100–200 ms, which read as a **hard cut**.
  > Default is now `exitMode: 'end'`; `exitMode: 'tail'` restores the crossfade (still with a fixed fade).
- Backdrop: silent, looping, `object-fit: cover`, with the **canvas and sidebar** surface tokens made
  translucent — **the picture is clearly visible** and the text stays readable.
  **Raised surfaces stay opaque**: the kernel paints dialogs, popovers, menus, cards and the settings
  view with `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-1/2/3` (`_dialog_* { background: var(--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2) }`), so
  those tokens are deliberately **left untouched** — otherwise the scrolling text behind a dialog shows
  through it and neither layer is readable.

dsh-video-skin README · Screenshots (captured on this machine by `scripts/verify-browser.mjs`)：Settings view in dark theme. That layer used to be `layer-2` at alpha 0.36 (the worst case) and let the
chat text show straight through the dialog; it now keeps the kernel's native opaque colour.

dsh-video-skin README · Sound：The desktop shell sets no `webPreferences.autoplayPolicy`, so Electron's default
(`no-user-gesture-required`) applies: an unmuted `play()` succeeds and the boot animation starts with
sound. A plain browser (`dsh web` in Chrome) blocks unmuted autoplay by default; the runtime then
**falls back to muted playback** (never trapping you on a dead screen) and shows a **separate** sound
button in the bottom-left — clicking it turns sound on without skipping, so the two intents never
collide. Set `boot.sound: false` for a silent boot.

dsh-video-skin README · Transparency：`surface` (dark theme) and `surfaceLight` (light theme) are the two knobs that trade picture strength
against readability; `veil` / `veilLight` are the scrims over the video. They are deliberately different
per theme: text is light in dark mode and dark in light mode, and this asset is dark (`YAVG ≈ 0.25`), so
an equally thin *white* surface drops dark text below 3:1. Measured in a real browser:

dsh-video-skin README · Tuning it in the UI：A small half-transparent pill sits in the bottom-right corner. Clicking it opens a panel with two
sliders (panel opacity / video scrim), three presets, a **live body-text contrast readout** measured from
the current video frame, and a reset button.

dsh-video-skin README · Tuning it in the UI：- Dragging applies immediately; releasing writes to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-video-skin.json` through a
  `POST`/`DELETE /dsh-video-skin/override` route. Only those four knobs are written; everything else in
  the file is preserved. A **refresh** picks the values up (no DSH restart), and the file stays
  hand-editable.
- A file rather than `localStorage`: the desktop page is served from the `dsh-app://` scheme, where Web
  Storage availability is not guaranteed.
- If the write fails (read-only home), the panel says so — it does not pretend to have saved.
- `Esc` or a click outside closes the panel; `Alt+B` toggles it; `background.controls: false` removes it.
- The pill sits at `z-index: 900`, **below** the kernel's `Modal` overlay (1000) on purpose: a modal
  should cover everything, and a wallpaper control must not steal its clicks.

dsh-video-skin README · Install：```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1     # writes profile package.json + bundles
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\uninstall.ps1   # removes both again
```

dsh-video-skin README · Install：**A full restart of DSH is required.** The desktop (Electron) shell serves a static `index.html` and
collects the index-injection table **once at host startup**, with no refresh path; `tapIndex` never
applies there. So a newly installed plugin's injection rows only reach the page on the next launch.

dsh-video-skin README · Configure：Defaults work as shipped. To tune, write either file (the second wins):

- `<plugin>/video-skin.config.json`
- `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\dsh-video-skin.json`

Changes apply on page refresh. On the desktop shell the boot-animation fields are baked into the
startup snapshot, so those need a restart.

dsh-video-skin README · How it is wired：```
Host half
  ├─ ctx.on('webserver/index-inject', table => table.push(styleRow, scriptRow))  ← first thing in apply()
  └─ ctx.inject(['webServer'], …) → /dsh-video-skin/{boot.mp4,background.mp4,config.json}
                                    with Range / ETag / 206 / 416 / HEAD

Three constraints that must not be broken (each one was paid for):

dsh-video-skin README · How it is wired：1. **Never `kind:'script-src'`.** The desktop interpreter `await`s external script rows and a rejection
   kills `__DSH_BOOT_READY__`, i.e. the whole app fails to start. An inline `kind:'script'` row cannot fail.
2. **Register the injection listener synchronously in `apply()`.** An object-level `inject` delays `apply`
   past the host's one-shot collection, and the row then never lands.
3. **Keep the overlay on `document.body`, never inside `#root`.** The kernel hydrates `#root`'s existing
   boot DOM (`:scope > [data-dsh-boot]`); inserting a node there breaks hydration.

dsh-video-skin README · How it is wired：The backdrop is a `position: fixed; z-index: -1` first child of `body`, so nothing in the app needs a
`z-index` and no pointer interaction is blocked.

dsh-video-skin README · Verify：```powershell
node scripts/check-syntax.mjs
node --test "tests/**/*.test.mjs"
node scripts/verify-all.mjs
```

dsh-video-skin README · Verify：`tests/runtime.test.mjs` runs the injected script inside a stub DOM with a virtual clock and asserts the
real timing properties (the clip plays to `ended` before the fade; the fade span is always the configured
`fadeMs`, never the remaining time; a click uses
`skipFadeMs`; **unmuted is tried first and muted is the fallback**; the sound button toggles sound
without skipping; the volume fades to 0 with the picture; unknown duration / no first frame / media
error (retried once) / a never-ready kernel each have an upper bound that never truncates the clip).
`tests/host.test.mjs` drives the real `apply()`
against a real HTTP server for the Range, `ETag`, `304`, `416` and cache-header contracts.
